Craft is a note-taking and productivity software application developed by Craft Docs Ltd., a software company located in Budapest, Hungary. The app was initially launched for macOS and iOS in November 2020, and later versions have been released for Windows, Android, and the web. In 2021, Apple awarded it the title of Mac App of the Year.
History
Bálint Orosz founded the company in 2019. Before this, he was Head of Product for Mobile at Skyscanner. Orosz's first introduction to the tech industry was when his startup Distinction was acquired by Skyscanner in 2014. The app was made publicly available on November 12, 2020. In his review for MacStories, Ryan Alessi mentioned that focusing on the native platform integration and being usable offline were two of the main reasons that the app was different from web-based tools like Notion.
Craft raised $8 million in Series A funding in April 2021, in a round led by Creandum with backing from InReach Ventures and Gareth Williams, co-founder of Skyscanner. TechCrunch called the group of investors a "Skyscanner Mafia" since a good number of the ex-Skyscanner executives got involved. That December, Apple picked Craft for Mac App of the Year at its annual App Store Awards. Sifted, a Financial Times-supported European technology publication, in 2021 featured Craft among the central European startups to watch, highlighting its popularity among knowledge workers.
In 2022, the company launched web and Windows app versions. A $12.2 million Series B round led by EBRD Venture Capital increased external investment to nearly $20 million. At that point, the company claimed over one million installations. Forbes Hungary also wrote about the round, calling Craft a "leading Hungarian startup."
Version 3, which came out in November 2024, introduced document styling features, collections, and task management integrated with a calendar. David Pierce from The Verge said that it was "shockingly close to my ideal productivity app." By September 2025, an update incorporated Apple's Liquid Glass aesthetics as well as on-device AI through Apple Foundation Models.
Functionality
Craft operates with a block-based editor through which users can prepare their documents by placing individual blocks of text, images, code, or other content. In addition, pages can be nested, arranged in folders, and interlinked. A single file can be converted into Markdown, PDF, or Microsoft Word formats, and multiple users can simultaneously edit a document.
With version 3, task management inside documents was implemented along with features like checklists, due dates, and reminders that are connected to the calendar view. An AI assistant capable of text generation, proofreading, translation, and summarization is available. It employs cloud processing or on-device models such as Apple Foundation Models.
Reception
Fast Company regarded Craft as "a great all-in-one productivity tool," mainly highlighting the strength of its visual design and collaboration features. Pocket-lint stated that the app is a great choice "for visual thinkers and designers," noting that it departs from the database-centric approach of Notion. One of XDA Developers' authors, comparing Microsoft OneNote and Craft, said that the latter had a more polished native interface but came at a higher price. MakeUseOf considered Craft as a tool that has become the note-taking solution of choice for people who wanted a simpler and more focused writing experience, rather than one that has "lost its way in the weeds of enterprise complexity," as Notion has. TechRadar suggested the app to people who want to keep their notes and documents organized inside a single tool.
The app has gotten a number of design awards, among them a German Design Award for Interactive User Experience and a German Brand Award. Besides that, Craft won Webby Awards back to back in 2024 and 2025, and was selected as one of the finalists of the Apple Design Awards in 2021.
Platform availability
Craft is available as a native app on macOS, iOS, iPadOS, and Windows, whereas the Android version is currently in beta. A web-based version is also available. All platforms work offline, with changes syncing across devices once a connection is restored.
